notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); every gate G1-G9 passed and the check report lists no warning. Nothing ran on a microscope: native.py and the PyUSB transport are untested, and the package is model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by stays null). The upstream clone has no stop command and does not brake the stage, so the @estop only disables the light and the shutter; no independent hardware e-stop is claimed, and a stage motion already sent is not stopped. The stage writes x, y and z are Limit.operator_required because the clone only queries the installed stage bounds (get_x_bounds/get_y_bounds/get_z_bound); site-limits.example.json is an example overlay with operator values, not device facts, and until an operator supplies site-limits.json every stage write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. NOT COVERED: the label and objective-metadata getters (get_condenser_labels, get_filter_labels, get_optical_path_labels, get_zoom_labels, get_objective_infos; each upstream getter issues one request per element), set_button_function (the clone documents the index range but no function codes), and image capture (the clone has no camera or image API). The fake starts from placeholder values (each marked # placeholder) and is not a recording of a device. MOCK PATH: the card's mock_strategy has no hints and no upstream tests, so the package ships an in-memory fake that defines only upstream method names (G7). check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
